proof_scope: In progress. R1769 proves integration by parts against Schwartz tests for functions and derivatives in L2 without an L1 assumption. A weak derivative represented by an L2 class gives the actual Fourier representative identity F(df)(xi)=2*pi*i*xi*F(f)(xi), exact derivative energy, and integrability of the weighted Fourier energy. The actual high-frequency component satisfies (2*pi*R)||P_high f||<=||df|| for R>=0 and the divided bound for R>0. These results are connected to the existing complexified Mobius action on Schwartz inputs, with null-set transport proved for arbitrary real normed target spaces. Iterated transported derivatives have the expected Fourier powers. The high-frequency energy is bounded by the four explicit spatial moments from R1768. Low-frequency orthogonality gives |<W_g u,h>_real|<=||D_g u||_2*||h||_2/(2*pi*R) whenever Fh vanishes on [-R,R]. Smooth band construction, square-summed moment estimates and band isolation remain.
next:
Construct actual smooth frequency-band pieces directly as inverse Fourier transforms of chi_j times the classical Fourier transform of the original unit-supported L2 input. First prove all spatial moments of that input are L1 and L2 with bounds inherited from support in [0,1]; use Real.contDiff_fourier and Real.iteratedDeriv_fourier to make its transform smooth. Multiplication by a smooth compactly supported cutoff then embeds in Schwartz space via HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap; inverse Fourier preserves Schwartz. Identify the resulting L2 class with the intended frequency multiplier using the proved L1/L2 bridge. This avoids building an unnecessary mixed L1-L2 convolution library.

For quantitative localization, exploit Fourier derivatives of chi_j*Ff and the finite-overlap dyadic supports. The key target is a square-sum bound on 2^(-2j)*||D_g u_j||_2^2 in terms of ||f||_2^2 and bounded matrix/cutoff constants, using the L2 bounds on Ff and its first two derivatives. Keep the actual norm dependence: no uniform estimate ||D_g u_j||<=C*2^j*||u_j|| is assumed. Combine the new separated-correlation bound with Cauchy-Schwarz over bands and the summable 2^(j-k) factor for k well above j; use symmetry for the other half. Obtain an explicit finite separation width making the far-band total small, then isolate a band with substantial action. Reuse all verified action, derivative, pole and Fourier support results. Flattening, generator existence, full motion/recursion and final referees remain required.
